extracted.intended_audience: faculty-led university research teams preparing white papers/proposals for the FY25 MURI (AFOSR/ARO/ONR) solicitation
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare multidisciplinary MURI white papers/proposals that align with specific FY25 topic objectives (AFOSR/ARO/ONR), meet scope and resource constraints, and address the listed research concentration areas and technical requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: energy–information relationships in biology
rubrics_metrics.description: This topic aims to support investigations of relationships between energy consumption and information processing in biological organisms with a goal of identifying strategies that could have implications for human and computer performance in energy-constrained environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should target understanding strategies organisms use to trade energy for information-processing performance and implications for engineered systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-scale energetic considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers should consider energetic requirements for information processing across the spectrum from cellular or subcellular levels to integrated sensory, cognitive, and motor systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should span or explicitly justify the chosen scale(s); experimental data collection methods may include electrophysiology, optical I/O, chemical analyses, genetics, and appropriate theory/modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify definition and measures of information
rubrics_metrics.description: There are multiple ways to define and quantify information. Proposers should specify their definition and associated measure(s) based on appropriateness for their research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State explicitly which information metric(s) are used and why they are appropriate for the hypotheses and experiments; tie metrics to interpretability and comparability across studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area: energy–precision tradeoff strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Information processing strategies observed in biological organisms that trade reduced energy consumption or metabolic demands with graceful degradations in computation and information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate observed biological strategies (e.g., reduced coding precision during scarcity) and analyze mechanisms and consequences for behavior and computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area: metabolic cost per information bit
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors impacting the metabolic/energetic cost of an information bit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify or model the energetic cost of bits in relevant systems; include measurement approaches and uncertainty analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area: biophysically-realistic model predictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Predictions from biophysically-realistic models of information processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and validate models grounded in measured biophysics; connect model predictions to experimental observables and energetic budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area: implications for human perceptual/cognitive performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Implications for human perceptual and cognitive performance under moderate to severe caloric restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate biological findings to hypotheses about human perception/cognition where appropriate; include behavioral metrics and ethical considerations for human studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research concentration area: information-theory-based computational strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Information theory-based computational strategies for artificial systems in energy-constrained conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose algorithms or architectures for engineered systems inspired by biological energy–information tradeoffs; include performance/efficiency analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources: budget and team-size caps (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no larger than $1.5M per year for five years and fund no more than six faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chiefs during the white paper phase of the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 4 Objective: conserved rules of biological assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of this MURI is to elucidate the fundamentally conserved rules of biological assembly of structural multifunctional materials with extreme mechanical properties and understand how these rules have been tuned through evolutionary processes across species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should focus on underlying rules and evolutionary tuning rather than solely on end-state characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 4 Research area: comparative assessment across species
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative assessment of extreme structural materials (e.g. bone, shell, exoskeleton) across species that display similar functionality/adaptation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include cross-species comparisons that link structure to function and evolutionary context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 4 Research area: cellular energetics and physical forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental assessment of the cellular energetics, resources, and physical forces (mechanical, electrical, thermal) that determine form and rate of biological material assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure or model the energetic/force constraints during assembly processes and relate to resulting structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 4 Research area: identify novel/conserved assembly molecules
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of novel and/or conserved proteins/molecules used in structural assembly, born out of evolutionary pressure, that enabled species survival in unique environments (biomineralization, scaffold construction, materials assembly, material degradation/recycling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use molecular, genetic and comparative approaches to find components responsible for assembly and durability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 4 Research area: methods to track materials creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Novel methods that combine molecular recognition and biotechnology modification of living systems to track materials creation at the molecular and macroscale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop or adapt imaging/labeling/genetic methods (AFM, CryoEM, NLO microscopy, etc.) suitable for multi-scale tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 4 Research area: models describing assembly processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation of informed models describing the process of structural material assembly at the molecular level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models should connect molecular interactions to macroscopic material properties and be testable experimentally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 4 Research area: demonstrate rules-based synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstration of 'rules' based synthesis of hybrid composite materials by synthetic and/or living systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate discovered rules into synthetic or engineered demonstrations that reproduce targeted properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentive: HBCU/MI participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for Topic 4 (and other topics) are invited that include participation from eligible HBCUs/MIs; HBCU/MI participation is not a requirement, but applications with an HBCU/MI MURI team member may be eligible for $1.5M in total additional funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams should consult Section I. Overview for HBCU/MI definitions and discuss eligibility; inclusion is incentivized but optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 5 Objective: mathematical control/systems framework for soft robotics
rubrics_metrics.description: This MURI topic seeks a novel mathematical data-driven and model-based control and systems theory framework designed for soft robotics that is amenable to reduced order modeling, uncertainty quantification and propagation and mathematical guarantees for control systems requirements of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks should address soft-robot-specific challenges: underactuation, unobservable states, environment interaction, and model uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 5 requirement: address robustness, safety, observability, controllability
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues such as robustness to uncertainty, and formal safety, ideas of observability/controllability, inverse kinematics, and stabilizability/detectability, should also be considered in the mathematical framework with attention to articulation of complexity in computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should include analyses or proofs concerning these properties and discuss computational tractability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 5 Research area: modeling framework amenable to control analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate a mathematical modeling framework for general soft robotics that is amenable to control theory and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer models that allow reduced-order approximations and are compatible with controller synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 5 Research area: uncertainty quantification and estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a rigorous framework for uncertainty quantification and state and parameter estimation of these systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include UQ methods, estimators/observers, and analysis of their performance under realistic noise and model error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 5 Research area: geometric inverse kinematics theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a geometric theory of inverse kinematics analogous to that of traditional robotics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop geometric or topological formulations suitable for continuum/soft-body configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 5 Research area: rigorous proofs backed by experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide formal and rigorous proofs of these systems behaviors backed up with experimental results including the interrelationships between sensing, actuation and locomotion of robotic modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link theory to demonstrators or experimental validation; include metrics comparing theory and experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 5 preference: consider environment-induced material changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference will be given to proposals for which the possible changes in material parameters (i.e., internal variables) induced by the environment are also considered in the approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address parameter sensitivity and environmental susceptibility in modeling and control designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 6 Objective: discover/modulate unconventional order parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: The goals of this topic are to (1) discover and explore novel, unconventional order parameters in quantum materials to concurrently break time-reversal and inversion symmetry, and (2) modulate these order parameters for tunability of Josephson diodes without external magnetic fields, to produce unprecedented high frequency functionalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should target physical mechanisms enabling superconducting diode effects and tunable device behavior without applied magnetic fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 6 Research area: discover/exploit order parameters to tune SDE
rubrics_metrics.description: Discover and exploit unconventional order parameters to tune the superconducting diode effect (e.g. asymmetry in the critical currents when the polarity of electric voltage is reversed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore candidate materials/systems and control knobs (gating, doping, architecture) that tune nonreciprocity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 6 Research area: elucidate mechanisms and limits of nonreciprocity
rubrics_metrics.description: Elucidate fundamental mechanisms and limits for the origins of the nonreciprocity of superconductivity, ideally under zero magnetic field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include theoretical and experimental studies identifying necessary symmetry breaking and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 6 Research area: diagnostics to probe mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply or develop diagnostics to probe and verify underlying mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose or use measurement techniques and metrology suitable for detecting order parameters and nonreciprocal transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 6 Research area: physics-based modeling of high-frequency dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop physics-based methods to model and exploit high frequency dynamics and functionalities in tunable Josephson diodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model device operation at relevant frequencies and predict performance for potential applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 7 Objective: fundamental study of N-qubit gates (beyond hardware fidelity)
rubrics_metrics.description: This topic seeks a deep and thorough basic research investigation of the fundamental potential, costs, and tradeoffs brought by N-qubit gates for advancements in quantum algorithms and protocols. Simply improving hardware, e.g., the fidelity of N-qubit gates, is not of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must address conceptual, algorithmic, and systems-level tradeoffs rather than only incremental hardware fidelity improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 7 Research area: novel algorithms/protocols enabled by N-qubit gates
rubrics_metrics.description: Novel or more efficient quantum algorithms and protocols enabled by N-qubit gates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show algorithmic advantages, reductions in depth/parameter counts, or new protocol capabilities attributable to N-qubit gates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 7 Research area: unconventional N-qubit implementations
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploration of unconventional N-qubit gate implementations (e.g., qudits, native phenomena such as many-body interactions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate non-standard hardware or encoding strategies that naturally implement multi-qubit operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 7 Research area: analyze advantages/limits/scalability/costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of advantages, fundamental limitations, scalability and operational costs of N-qubit gate algorithms and protocols as compared to sequences decomposed into single and two-qubit gates for applications such as quantum error correction, fault-tolerant quantum information processing, quantum networking and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative comparisons (error budgets, resource counts, connectivity, overheads) versus conventional decompositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 7 Research area: noise channels and error budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding of noise channels and error budgets of N-qubit gate schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize dominant error sources, scaling with N, and mitigation strategies; include modeling and experiments where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 7 Research area: characterization, verification, validation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods to characterize, verify, and validate N-qubit gate approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop or adapt benchmarking, tomography, randomized protocols, or other validation techniques appropriate for multi-qubit gates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 7 Research area: experiments to inform theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments that can demonstrate or enhance theoretical insight into N-qubit gate-based algorithms and protocols early on in the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose experiments—even with small N—that elucidate tradeoffs, error behavior, or algorithmic impact; approaches should be scalable with N.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources: Topic 7 budget/team size
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than 5 funded faculty researchers. Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chief(s) during the white paper phase of the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan budgets/team composition accordingly and consult topic chiefs if larger resources are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 8 Objective: hot solid-state qubits at 300 mK–1 K with low error rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall objective of this MURI topic is to discover, design and demonstrate new Josephson junction and gated-defined quantum dot based qubits compatible with operation at temperatures in the regime 300 mK to 1 K, whilst maintaining low error-rate quantum operations (i.e., < 1% error for a universal set of qubit operations). Furthermore, qubits should be capable of running long sequences of gates without interference from initialization or reset requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should target demonstration/measurement of error rates (<1%) for universal gate sets and sustained operation over long sequences; include mechanisms to mitigate thermally-induced noise and loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 8 Research area: unconventional materials for higher-temperature qubits
rubrics_metrics.description: Study, design and fabrication of unconventional materials suitable for Josephson junction circuits or gate-defined quantum dot qubit operation at higher operational temperatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials research should focus on compatibility with low-loss qubit operation at elevated temperatures and identify loss mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 8 Research area: novel qubit energy-level designs for low-error reset
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of novel qubit designs with desirable energy-level structures to enable low-error rate reset methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs must support fast, low-error initialization and minimal disturbance to neighboring qubits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 8 Research area: engineering qubit environment to reduce thermal coupling
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineering of the qubit environment to reduce thermally-coupled noise due to the higher temperatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address phononic, piezoelectric, quasiparticle, and other temperature-dependent noise sources via materials, packaging, or shielding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 8 Research area: theory and modeling of thermally-induced loss
rubrics_metrics.description: Associated theory to include modeling of thermally-induced material loss mechanisms, device thermalization, advancing the understanding of non-linearities at high temperatures and developing, optimizing and studying the limits of active and initialization techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quantitative modeling of thermal processes and predictions that can be experimentally validated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 8 Research area: optimized control techniques for reset/operation/readout
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of optimized control techniques for active reset or optimized control techniques for qubit operation, initialization and readout with minimal side-effects on other qubits, and absence of noise or heat generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control methods should minimize cross-talk, heating, and disturbance to system coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 8 Research area: sympathetic/analogous cooling methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods analogous to sympathetic cooling with mixed species solid-state qubits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore helper devices or mixed-species approaches to remove excitations without disrupting computation; consider analogies to atomic sympathetic cooling and model potential interference with qubit operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 8 active-initialization cases to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should consider: a) rapid removal of excess thermal excitations and initialization prior to algorithms; b) active initialization/reset during algorithms while maintaining low operational error; c) 'selective cooling' initializing specific data qubits without affecting neighbors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and evaluate methods for each case, including dynamics, control overhead, and impacts on algorithm fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources: Topic 8 budget/team size
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting 5 or less faculty researchers and their associated students, postdocs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale team and budget requests accordingly; contact the Research Topic Chief for clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 9 Objective: QML for quantum data processing
rubrics_metrics.description: To develop and explore novel QML approaches to process quantum data, and to enable enhancements over the currently best quantum and classical methods. Specifically we envision exploiting quantum sensor data to avoid QRAM complications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on quantum-data-native QML that leverages quantum sensor outputs and analyze when quantum advantages are possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 9 Research area: analyze data types suited for QML
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental analysis of the types of data best suited for QML, collected from various quantum sensors either in local or distributed configurations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize data structure, noise, and sample complexity to assess amenability to QML speedups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 9 Research area: optimize QML platforms for sensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental analysis of and innovations in QML platforms and their optimization for quantum sensing applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop algorithms and hardware mappings optimized for processing quantum sensor outputs, including noise robustness and resource accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 9 Research area: compare quantum and classical ML operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for comparing fundamental operations in quantum and classical ML realms and their limitations, to better understand under what circumstances which approach is optimal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide theoretical and empirical comparisons, including cost of quantization/encoding and end-to-end performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 9 Research area: optimal data collection methods for QML
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimal methods of collecting either static or time dependent data amenable for QML processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design sensing/measurement strategies that maximize downstream QML accuracy or efficiency; consider ensemble sizes and temporal sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated resources: Topic 9 budget/team size
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than an average of $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than 6 funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for multi-investigator teams within these bounds and justify exceptions with topic chiefs if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-level pattern: multidisciplinary and team expertise expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Many topics require multidisciplinary expertise (e.g., biology, neuroscience, biophysics, information theory; control theory, robotics, materials science; quantum algorithms and experimentalists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble teams with complementary expertise named in each topic; describe roles and integration across disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal scalability requirement (where stated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where relevant, proposed approaches should be scalable (e.g., N-qubit gate proposals should be scalable with N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how methods/experiments/theory generalize beyond small proof-of-concept settings and address scaling constraints.
